scenes.title: Cold open
narration: Nine Circles to the Sun
This is Ohuokhai (Osuokhai). Ancient.

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance has roots in the period when the Sakha people lived further south as cattle-breeders.
It is historically linked to the Yhyakh festival, which celebrates the summer solstice.
Following a period of stagnation, the 21st century saw a revival of the tradition.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is performed during the Yhyakh festival to celebrate the summer solstice, the triumph of life, and the rebirth of nature.
It symbolizes the circle of life and the capturing of solar energy.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers form a circle, holding each other by the hand or arm.
The movement is performed with the left foot placed forward, following a clockwise direction.
The dance is characterized by rhythmic, graceful movements of the body, legs, feet, and arms.
Watch for Clockwise Circle.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is improvisational, featuring a lead singer who composes poetry on the spot.
Key instruments include the chomus (scacciapensieri) and the kyrimpa (Yakut violin).
Listen for the chomus, kyrimpa.
A rhythmic, communal sound characterized by vocal improvisation and the vibration of the Kylyhakh technique, accompanied by the metallic twang of the chomus and the strings of the kyrimpa.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The dance is performed in an 'alas' (a large meadow), often near a 'World Tree' (Aal Luuk Mas).
Participants often wear traditional costumes during the Yhyakh festival.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Sergey Zverev, a folk singer, poet, and composer from the Suntarsky region, is noted for adding new elements to the expressiveness of the movements.
The dance is a native Sakha tradition, linked to the cult of the sun and fertility.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: The dance is associated with a solar deity and fertility cult; participants believe it allows them to capture the sun's energy for the year.
